licenses.text:
JPS TaNaKH 1917, eBible.org, https://ebible.org/engjps/

The edition's own statement of rights (from eBible.org's page for this translation):
> "Public Domain
Language: English
Dialect: American
Translation by: Jewish Publication Society
This copy of the Old JPS TaNaKH by the Jewish Publication Society is brought to you courtesy of eBible.org. For the new JPS TaNaKH (1972, 1978, 1980), please see jps.org."
(from eBible.org's page for this translation, https://ebible.org/engjps/copyright.htm)

Why this is public domain:
Translation by a committee of the Jewish Publication Society of America, an American publisher founded in Philadelphia, first published by it in 1917 (eBible's description: 'The Jewish Bible (Old Testament) in English, published by the Jewish Publication Society in 1917'). US: published in 1917, before 1931, so public domain in the United States. Origin country: the United States, the country of first publication, so the United States rule above settles it too. The later JPS translation (1972 to 1985) is a different text and is not used here.

Sources of these facts:
eBible.org copyright page (https://ebible.org/engjps/copyright.htm) and details page (https://ebible.org/details.php?id=engjps); the 1917 publication from English Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_Publication_Society_of_America_Version: 'The translation, which appeared in 1917'), and the publisher's founding in Philadelphia from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_Publication_Society.

The verse-per-line archive holds the Bible text in one file, one verse per line, each line starting with its reference (book, chapter:verse); its SQL and XML copies of the same text, eBible.org's description page, style sheet and signature are left out of the source.

note: The verse-numbered twin of ebible-engjps-60669439, for the parallel verses measure only (#35): its tag is verse-numbers alone, which no mixture selects, so it never enters training. eBible.org rebuilds this zip often; the checksum covers the files inside.
